lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Put Harbor Payments before Crestline Logistics in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Harbor Payments is more recent, and recruiters expect reverse chronology.

items.says: Make the current diesel mechanic role support the product and operations narrative.
items.because: A post-MBA mechanic role may confuse recruiters unless it emphasizes transferable ownership, reliability, prioritization, and outcomes.

items.says: Make the food-rescue project clearly look like a genuine operating venture rather than a class exercise.
items.because: Its sustained ownership and shipped product are valuable for product applications.

items.says: Use consistent date punctuation, preferably en dashes instead of hyphens.
Prevent bullets from breaking awkwardly across lines in the final PDF.
Prioritize Harbor Payments and the food-rescue app visually and in detail.
items.because: They are the most relevant entries for product roles.

items.says: Keep the résumé to one page unless there is substantial additional relevant material.
Add a summary only if it efficiently explains the unusual career transition.
items.because: The progression from operations to MBA and product work to diesel mechanics may otherwise be confusing.

items.says: Tailor the skills and bullet emphasis toward product discovery, prioritization, experimentation, launch, adoption, and impact.
items.because: The résumé is being positioned for product roles.

items.says: Ensure the LinkedIn URL works.
Customize the LinkedIn URL.
Add a portfolio or project link only if it contains substantive product artifacts, case studies, or shipped work.
Add city and state only if location matters for the targeted roles.
items.because: Location in the header is optional.

items.says: Confirm that the phone number and email are professional and current.
Make the MBA completion status unmistakable if the degree is completed.
items.because: Recruiters should not have to infer completion from the dates.

items.says: Add a concentration, distinction, or leadership position only if it meaningfully supports the target role.
Consider showing only the graduation timing if space is needed.
items.because: The older degree does not require as much date detail.

items.says: Add a prior average, service target, or avoided downtime to contextualize the under-five-day turnaround.
items.because: The current metric does not show why that turnaround is strong.

items.says: Clarify whether the work was completed personally, led, or performed as part of a team.
items.because: The current wording may overstate individual ownership if the jobs were collaborative.

items.says: Add reliability, repeat-failure, or economic-impact metrics after repair.
items.because: Turnaround alone does not show repair quality.

items.says: Rewrite the bullet as an accomplishment rather than a routine responsibility.
items.because: It currently states maintenance and recordkeeping without showing what changed.

items.says: Add scale, inspection results, compliance, uptime, defects prevented, or issues identified.
items.because: The bullet lacks a measurable result.

items.says: Reduce the emphasis on recordkeeping unless it materially improved inspections or compliance.
Replace responsibility language with the decisions or improvements enabled by the scorecards.
items.because: The bullet says what was managed but not what changed.

items.says: Quantify the scorecards' scope using carriers, regions, managers, shipment volume, or spend.
Explain whether the scorecards improved service, cost, delivery, claims, or carrier accountability.
Replace or clarify the vague phrase about the monthly meeting discussing the scorecards.
items.because: It adds little without an outcome.

items.says: Add the period over which the 30% error reduction was measured.
Add the baseline pick-error rate.
items.because: A relative reduction without a baseline is difficult to evaluate.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction was sustained after retraining.
Add any downstream effect on labor cost, rework, complaints, or order accuracy.
Define whether forecast error was MAPE, bias, or another standard metric.
Specify the business scope by product categories, revenue, facilities, or region.
Remove the 12-consecutive-quarters detail if space is tight.
items.because: Business scale is more important than the consistency detail.

items.says: Clarify whether the consensus-forecast process was created or merely facilitated.
Reduce the number of separate activities packed into the bullet.
items.because: It combines implementation, SOPs, training, vendor negotiations, and labor savings.

items.says: Choose whether operational rollout or vendor management is the central achievement.
items.because: The current bullet lacks a clear emphasis.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 saved hours came from route optimization, process changes, or both.
items.because: The attribution is unclear.

items.says: Add adoption, driver count, route volume, cost savings, or service-level impact.
Clarify whether all 2,300 merchants used the redesigned process or were only part of the broader pilot population.
Specify ownership across discovery, requirements, coordination, experimentation, launch, or analysis.
Include stable fraud, compliance, or approval-quality guardrails if applicable.
items.because: The one-step verification process may have involved tradeoffs.

items.says: Clarify whether the conversion increase was statistically reliable.
State the A/B test period.
State that the directly measured conversion effect was session-level.
items.because: Randomization occurred by session, not by unique customer.

items.says: Explain how repeat users appearing in both variants were handled analytically.
Using support tickets each feature would close as RICE Reach is methodologically incorrect.
items.because: Reach should be a population such as users, merchants, or transactions affected over a defined period, while tickets closed is closer to outcome or impact.

items.says: Define the period used for Reach.
items.because: RICE scores are not meaningful without a time horizon.

items.says: Remove the RICE reference if the scoring cannot be made methodologically sound.
items.because: Highlighting unsound scoring may signal weak product-method knowledge.

items.says: Add the decision or outcome produced by the prioritization.
items.because: Applying a framework is weaker than showing what decision it changed.

items.says: The sentence lacks a clear subject and becomes grammatically indirect near the end.
Specify the problem or feature area that became the roadmap priority.
Explain how the interviews, chargeback analysis, and financial sizing affected the decision.
The roadmap-prioritization content overlaps with the preceding RICE bullet.
items.because: The two bullets should be consolidated unless they describe different decisions.

items.says: Retain the 25-interview count only if the sample represented the relevant segments reasonably well.
This bullet duplicates the earlier checkout-conversion experiment.
items.because: The same project should appear only once.

items.says: The causal claim assigns a session-randomized result to customers.
items.because: The directly measured effect is on sessions, not necessarily unique customers.

items.says: Do not generalize the result to all merchant customers without supporting analysis.
items.because: Session-level measurement alone does not support that inference.

items.says: Connect the funded expansion directly to the earlier onboarding initiative.
items.because: Recruiters should immediately understand that it was the downstream result of that work.

items.says: Clarify whether rollout to the additional regions occurred or was only approved.
Add later rollout results if they are available.
items.because: Actual results are stronger than stopping at approval.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 means registered users, eligible students, downloads, or active users.
Verify the nine-tonne figure and its measurement period.
Add specific product ownership such as requirements, design decisions, engineering coordination, or stakeholder management.
Avoid saying the food would have been thrown away unless waste diversion was directly measured.
items.because: Otherwise the claim may sound inferred.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Provide an experiment, phased rollout, cohort comparison, or pre/post method supporting the attribution to reminders.
items.because: User interviews can explain feature choice but do not prove that reminders caused the growth.

items.says: Clarify the period over which weekly active users increased.
The increase from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not 20%.
items.because: The relative increase would be 26.7%.

items.says: Explain how the volunteer shift system increased pickup-slot fill rate.
items.because: The mechanism is not immediately obvious.

items.says: Clarify whether the fill-rate result was sustained and over what period.
Connect the operational result more clearly to product ownership.
items.because: The bullet is operational rather than product-focused.

items.says: Change the singular “saving” to “savings.”
Clearly label the $2.4M as projected rather than realized savings.
items.because: The current wording could be read as an achieved financial result even though it came from a model.

items.says: Add major assumptions or cost categories behind the estimate.
items.because: They would establish the model's credibility.

items.says: Rewrite the bullet from passive voice to show clear ownership.
Add a measurable result such as reduced form length, processing time, errors, or staff effort.
Clarify whether adoption of the shortened form produced a demonstrated improvement.
Distinguish the team lead's contribution from the team's collective output.
The pilot approval duplicates the approval already mentioned in the first practicum bullet.
items.because: The approval should be consolidated into one place unless this bullet demonstrates a separate skill.

items.says: Focus on what changed because of the presentation rather than simply naming attendees.
Clarify whether the pilot was completed.
Add the pilot's results if they are available.
Retain only product skills that are supported by bullets elsewhere.
Make the A/B-testing claim credible by correcting the session-level experimental-practice issues.
Strengthen the roadmapping claim by fixing the RICE bullet and showing an actual prioritization decision.
Add other relevant product capabilities only if they are genuine.
items.because: Potential additions include product analytics, prioritization, market research, stakeholder management, and KPI definition.

items.says: List tool proficiency only when it is meaningful and defensible.
Reflect Amplitude in the experience or project bullets if it played a meaningful role.
Support the generic Excel listing with evidence of modeling, forecasting, or analysis.
items.because: Excel is more valuable when demonstrated through substantive work.
